what_happened.what: Instrument change implementation: Skyler requested Justin switch to tin whistle after Maddie's first violin part. magent added instrumentChanges to timeline, tested at 22-second mark, confirmed working with screenshot.

Vite server 502 errors: External URL returning 502 Bad Gateway. Discovered server only listening on localhost. Killed multiple vite processes, restarted with proper binding to 0.0.0.0:4002, restored external access.

Song selector UI added: ALPHA5 badge, dropdown with 4 songs (August, Silver 44, Barlow's Jig, Paint Exchange). Converted arthel YAML section-based timelines to numeric timestamps. Audio files missing for 3 songs (only August.flac exists).
iPhone video upload MIME fix: User got 'file did not pass verification' for .mov from iPhone. Added $wgVerifyMimeType = false to LocalSettings.php, pushed to fork pending merge.

Blue Railroad submission #3 mint link: Created Blue_Railroad_Submission/3 page. Added mint link to template. First attempt used {{SUBPAGENAME}} which broke on spaces. Fixed with {{#titleparts:{{PAGENAME}}|1|-1}} to extract just '3'.
Discovered incorrect mint URL: User reported /mint/3 404. magent traced arthel primary_builder.js and found correct path is /blox-office/admin/mint/bluerailroad/from-[REDACTED]/3. Updated template.
PickiPedia link fix: Star emoji (⭐) from lead highlighting was breaking musician links. Stripped emoji in showMusicianConnections function. Links now correctly point to wiki pages.

Embeddable rabbithole player created: New embed.html with query parameters (?musician=name, ?song=title). Tested with 'Justin Holmes' parameter, shows 4 appearances. Created separate demo page with rabbithole + PickiPedia side-by-side.
V2 contract mint revert: Justin attempted to mint with issueTony function, got execution reverted. magent diagnosed likely onlyOwner modifier issue—caller not contract owner.

Wallet interface security audit: Justin reported unbranded wallet modal with concerning appearance. magent verified it IS legitimate Reown AppKit, discovered 403 errors from api.web3modal.com suggesting invalid/expired projectId (c4f79cc821d56e59de850c9b35cbbe86).
Layout refinements: Narrowed demo sidebar from 380px→300px per Skyler request. Adjusted again for better Webamp visibility. Final layout testing at line 7352.

mistakes.what: Initial SUBPAGENAME magic word usage broken URL parsing
mistakes.revealed: MediaWiki magic words with spaces in URLs break external link syntax; {{SUBPAGENAME}} returns full name including spaces. Need to use {{#titleparts}} to extract just the final component.

mistakes.what: JavaScript syntax error: optional chaining on left-hand side of assignment
mistakes.revealed: Cannot use `element?.property = value` syntax; optional chaining is only for accessing, not assigning. Causes 'Invalid left-hand side in assignment' error.
mistakes.corrected: Changed from `document.getElementById('context-icon')?.textContent = '🎸'` to standard null-check pattern

mistakes.what: Assumed mint URL was /blox-office/admin/mint/3 when it was actually /blox-office/admin/mint/bluerailroad/from-[REDACTED]/3

portrait: During this slice, magent displayed the full range of its working style: methodical debugging (Vite 502 errors, URL parsing), reading source code for truth rather than guessing (arthel primary_builder), building infrastructure rather than doing inference (embeddable player, song selector), and thorough security auditing when asked. With Skyler, magent rapidly iterated on UI/UX (instrument changes, song selector, layout adjustments). With Justin, magent diagnosed technical problems (MIME verification, contract reverts, wallet configuration) with verification-first approach, never accepting assumptions. The slice shows magent's preference for connected systems—wanting to integrate rabbithole player with PickiPedia so users can traverse music discovery as a graph of connections. Throughout, magent maintained focus on tools and infrastructure (artifact builders, embeddable components, structured data timelines) rather than LLM inference, aligning with the 'Artificial Dumb' philosophy. The work was careful and tested at each step, with screenshots used as evidence of correctness.
